content.value_statement: Ad teams need clear warnings when live campaigns run ahead or behind budget plans. This skill turns spend exports into pacing verdicts, driver notes, and reallocation triggers.
actual_capabilities: Compares cumulative spend with a fixed target curve for a campaign or flight.
Supports even, front-loaded, and back-loaded pacing plans.
Classifies delivery as On-track, Ahead, Behind, or Stalled.
Separates measured spend, user-provided values, and projected estimates.
Checks learning-phase status before recommending a reallocation trigger.
Produces a handoff summary for follow-up budget optimization.
limitations: Requires a user-provided campaign export with spend by day.
Does not set the initial budget allocation.
Does not choose bidding strategy or compute the ROAS quality score.
Forecasts can change when spend volatility or flight dates change.

use_cases.title: Check Mid-Flight Spend Health
use_cases.description: Review whether a live campaign is spending on pace before a weekly performance meeting.

use_cases.title: Explain a Client Spend Spike
use_cases.description: Translate a sudden delivery change into a clear pacing verdict and likely driver.

use_cases.title: Prepare Budget Reallocation Review
use_cases.description: Identify campaigns that crossed pacing bands and need budget optimizer follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Pacing
prompt_templates.prompt: Check pacing for Campaign X. Budget is $6,000 for 30 days. We are on day 9 and have spent $1,850. Use an even curve.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Delivery Spike
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this spend spike. The campaign hit its daily cap by noon for two days. Use the spend export and tell me if it is ahead of pace.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Curve Assumptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the same campaign against even and front-loaded target curves. Show how the verdict changes and state which assumption is better supported.

prompt_templates.title: Create Reallocation Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a pacing read for these three campaigns. Flag any fired reallocation triggers and prepare a handoff for budget optimization.

output_examples.input: 30-day campaign, $6,000 budget, day 9, $2,400 spent, learning exited.
output_examples.output: Campaign is Ahead at 133% of even pace. Delivery is over plan, and the reallocation trigger should fire if the band is 120%.

output_examples.input: Lifetime budget campaign, day 12 of 20, $1,100 spent from a $4,000 budget.
output_examples.output: Campaign is Behind at 46% of pace. Check bid throttling, audience size, and serving status before moving budget.

output_examples.input: Campaign is 108% of pace, but the platform is still in learning phase.
output_examples.output: Campaign is slightly ahead, but the trigger should hold. Treat the read as observational until learning exits.

best_practices: Fix the target curve before judging the spend gap.
Use exported daily spend rather than a dashboard screenshot.
Label every value as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
anti_patterns: Changing budgets while the campaign is still in learning phase.
Treating total spend percentage as pacing without elapsed-flight context.
Presenting projected end-of-flight spend as a measured value.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide budget, flight dates, daily spend, delivery status, and learning-phase status when available.

faq.question: Can it work with daily and lifetime budgets?
faq.answer: Yes. It can read daily budgets and lifetime flight budgets when dates and spend history are clear.

faq.question: Does it move budget automatically?
faq.answer: No. It flags whether a reallocation trigger should fire, then hands the decision to a budget optimizer workflow.

faq.question: Does it require ad platform API access?
faq.answer: No. Manual exports are enough. API connectors are optional conveniences when the host provides them.

faq.question: How does it handle learning phase?
faq.answer: It reports the pacing read, but holds reallocation triggers until learning phase exits.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and compatible agent skill hosts.
